text: The present study was designed to address this gap by integrating emotional, behavioral, and coping dimensions into a unified analytical framework. Using multivariate analyses and structural equation modelling, the study sought to: (1) estimate the prevalence and severity of childhood anxiety using the RCMAS-2 ( 11 ); (2) examine how internalizing, externalizing, prosocial behavior, and coping patterns relate to anxiety; and (3) test a structural model assessing direct and indirect pathways linking behavioral tendencies, coping style, and contextual factors to anxiety outcomes.
source_label: Coping and behavior as predictors of childhood anxiety: an SEM-based analysis in school-going children
